newsitem.title: TURKEY: U.S. envoy says Cyprus missile mission a success.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy says Cyprus missile mission a success.

text.p: U.S. envoy Carey Cavanaugh said on Thursday his mission to dampen down a row between Turkey and its Greek adversaries over the deployment of anti-aircraft missiles on Cyprus had been a success.

"This visit has turned out to be a successful diplomatic mission in what the United States was concerned could have been a crisis atmosphere," Cavanaugh told a news conference in the Turkish capital after trips to Cyprus and Athens.

Cavanaugh said he had told the Cypriot government of U.S. opposition to the missile deal. "I think that message has been delivered," he said. He also passed on Washington's concern to Turkey about threats to use force to halt the missiles arriving.
State Department official Cavanaugh on Wednesday predicted the planned deployment of the Russian S-300 missiles would not take place.
Earlier, he said the crisis had been defused because Greek Cypriot authorities had assured him they would not bring in any part of the $426 million missile system for at least 16 months.

Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkey invaded the north of the island after a coup in Nicosia engineered by Athens. Turkey has around 30,000 troops in the north while the internationally recognised Cypriot government, which has a military pact with Athens, has 11,500 in the south.
